related_questions.question: What are the AHA guidelines for CPR?

text_blocks.snippet: The American Heart Association (AHA) provides comprehensive guidelines for cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR), emphasizing high-quality chest compressions and timely defibrillation. For healthcare providers, the guidelines generally involve a 30:2 compression-to-breath ratio for adults. For the general public, Hands-Only CPR (chest compressions without rescue breaths) is recommended for sudden cardiac arrest in adults and teens.

list.snippet: Depth: At least 2 inches (5 cm) for adults, and at least one-third the depth of the chest in infants and children.
Rate: 100-120 compressions per minute.
Recoil: Allow for full chest recoil after each compression to allow the heart to refill with blood.
Minimizing Interruptions: Reduce pauses in compressions as much as possible, aiming for less than 10 seconds.
For trained individuals, use a 30:2 compression-to-breath ratio for adults.
For trained individuals, two breaths after every 30 chest compressions.
Recommended for the public in cases of witnessed sudden cardiac arrest in adults and teens.
Focuses solely on chest compressions without rescue breaths until emergency help arrives.
Use an automated external defibrillator (AED) as soon as it is available.
Follow the AED's voice prompts for rhythm analysis and defibrillation.
Immediately call 911 or your local emergency number when cardiac arrest is suspected.
If alone, activate emergency services before starting CPR.
High-quality CPR includes adequate compression depth, rate, and minimal interruptions.
Early defibrillation with high-quality CPR is crucial for survival in cases of shockable rhythms.
For healthcare providers, the guidelines address various scenarios, including advanced airway management and asynchronous ventilation.
The guidelines also address situations such as opioid-associated cardiac arrest.

list.snippet: For adults, children, and infants, a single rescuer should perform 30 chest compressions followed by 2 rescue breaths.

list.title: Two-Rescuer CPR:
list.snippet: In cases where two people are performing CPR on an infant, the ratio changes to 15 compressions to 2 breaths.

list.title: Focus on Compressions:
list.snippet: The current guidelines emphasize the importance of continuous chest compressions and minimizing interruptions during CPR.

list.title: AED Use:
list.snippet: If an automated external defibrillator (AED) is available, it should be used as soon as possible.

list.title: When to Stop:
list.snippet: CPR should be continued until one of the following occurs: the person shows signs of life, an AED is ready to use, another trained rescuer takes over, EMS personnel arrive, or the rescuer is too exhausted to continue, according to the American Red Cross.
